quests.instruction: At the airport gate, a worker scans boarding passes, answers questions about the flight, and announces when passengers can board. Who is it?
options: Gate Agent
Baggage Handler
Pilot
quests.correctAnswer: Gate Agent
quests.hint: Think about the person at the desk beside the door to the plane.
quests.explanation: Gate agents check boarding passes, help passengers, and make announcements so boarding runs smoothly.
quests.funFact: Gate agents often call passengers to board in groups so the aisle does not get crowded.

quests.instruction: In a busy hospital, someone pushes patients in wheelchairs to the X-ray room and carries samples to the lab. Who is it?
options: Receptionist
Hospital Dietitian
Hospital Porter
quests.correctAnswer: Hospital Porter
quests.hint: Think about someone who moves patients and items around the building.
quests.explanation: Hospital porters move patients, equipment, and samples around large buildings so everything arrives where it is needed.
quests.funFact: Hospitals can be as large as small towns, so porters help things reach the right place.

quests.instruction: At the end of a busy dinner service, someone washes the pots, pans, and plates so the cooks can start fresh tomorrow. Who is it?
options: Restaurant Waiter
Kitchen Porter
Head Chef
quests.correctAnswer: Kitchen Porter
quests.hint: Think about someone who keeps pots, pans, and plates clean and ready.
quests.explanation: Kitchen porters wash dishes and equipment and keep the kitchen tidy, which lets the cooks focus on preparing food.
quests.funFact: Commercial dishwashers use very hot water to clean large numbers of plates quickly.

quests.instruction: At a busy restaurant, two cooks call in sick. Who decides how to reorganize the team so service keeps running?
options: Cashier
Shift Manager
Customer Service Worker
quests.correctAnswer: Shift Manager
quests.hint: Think about the person in charge of the team for today.
quests.explanation: Shift managers lead a team during their shift and make quick decisions when plans change.
quests.funFact: Many workplaces use a rota, a list that shows who works each shift.

quests.instruction: In a TV studio, a worker moves a big camera smoothly to follow the presenter while the director gives instructions. Who is it?
options: Camera Operator
Photographer
Sound Engineer
quests.correctAnswer: Camera Operator
quests.hint: Think about someone who controls the filming equipment during a live program.
quests.explanation: Camera operators follow directions from the director and move cameras smoothly to capture what viewers will see.
quests.funFact: Studio cameras often sit on wheeled stands so operators can glide smoothly.

quests.instruction: During a play, someone backstage calls when the lights should change, tells actors when to enter, and keeps everything on schedule. Who is it?
options: Lighting Operator
Lead Actor
Stage Manager
quests.correctAnswer: Stage Manager
quests.hint: Think about the person who keeps the whole show running on time.
quests.explanation: Stage managers coordinate everyone backstage, give cues, and keep the performance running on time.
quests.funFact: Stage managers often follow a script marked with every cue for lights, sounds, and entrances.

quests.instruction: At a large dairy farm, a worker checks that the milk is cooled and stored at the right temperature before the truck arrives. Who is in charge of this stage?
options: Bread Baker
Tractor Driver
Dairy Worker
quests.correctAnswer: Dairy Worker
quests.hint: Think about someone who looks after milk on a farm.
quests.explanation: Dairy workers help milk cows, keep equipment clean, and make sure the milk is stored safely.
quests.funFact: Milk must be kept cold so that it stays fresh and safe to drink.

quests.instruction: At a busy harbor, someone decides which ship docks where, and in what order, so that ships do not crash. Who is it?
options: Harbor Master
Fishing Boat Captain
Lifeboat Crew
quests.correctAnswer: Harbor Master
quests.hint: Think about the traffic planner for the port.
quests.explanation: Harbor masters manage ship traffic in a port, assign docking spaces, and keep the harbor safe.
quests.funFact: Harbors use marked channels and signals to guide ships safely.

quests.instruction: In a power plant control room, a worker watches many screens to make sure the electricity supply stays steady. Who is it?
options: Power Line Worker
Control Operator
House Electrician
quests.correctAnswer: Control Operator
quests.hint: Think about someone who monitors a whole system from a room full of screens.
quests.explanation: Control operators watch screens and readings, notice changes quickly, and adjust the system to keep power steady.
quests.funFact: Control rooms for important services are often staffed day and night.

quests.instruction: A cleaner in a hospital notices liquid spilled in a busy hallway. What is the best thing to do?
options: Put up a sign and clean it up
Walk past without saying a word
Cover the spill with a small mat
quests.correctAnswer: Put up a sign and clean it up
quests.hint: Think about protecting people from slipping.
quests.explanation: A warning sign tells people to take care, and cleaning the spill quickly prevents falls.
quests.funFact: Yellow warning signs are used in many countries to show that a floor is wet.

quests.instruction: A lifeguard supervisor notices that a lifeguard looks very tired after a long shift. What should the supervisor do?
options: Ask them to keep going without a rest
Arrange a break and a replacement
Tell them to look away from the water
quests.correctAnswer: Arrange a break and a replacement
quests.hint: Think about staying alert and keeping swimmers safe.
quests.explanation: Tired workers can miss important details, so supervisors arrange breaks and replacements to keep everyone safe.
quests.funFact: Lifeguards often rotate between positions so that they stay alert.

quests.instruction: Mail arrives at a sorting center in huge bags. What is the first job of the sorters?
options: Deliver every item to a door
Open each parcel to look inside
Sort items by where they are going
quests.correctAnswer: Sort items by where they are going
quests.hint: Think about directing each item to the right next truck.
quests.explanation: Sorters group letters and parcels by destination so they can be sent on the right routes.
quests.funFact: Many sorting centers use machines that read addresses to speed up the work.

quests.instruction: The school office learns that a child's parent will collect them early. Who should be told so the child is ready?
options: School Bus Driver
Class Teacher
School Cook
quests.correctAnswer: Class Teacher
quests.hint: Think about who is with the child during the day.
quests.explanation: The class teacher knows where the child is and can help them get ready, so passing on the message helps keep everyone organized.
quests.funFact: Schools keep clear records of who collects each child, to make sure pupils are safe.

quests.instruction: A museum guard sees a visitor reaching toward a display. What is the best thing to do?
options: Shout loudly across the whole room
Take every object out of the room
Politely remind them of the rules
quests.correctAnswer: Politely remind them of the rules
quests.hint: Think about being calm and respectful.
quests.explanation: Guards protect both objects and visitors by calmly reminding people of the rules.
quests.funFact: Oils from skin can slowly damage some museum objects.

quests.instruction: A storm delays several flights. What should the gate agent do?
options: Share clear updates with passengers
Tell passengers to ignore announcements
Lock the gate and walk away
quests.correctAnswer: Share clear updates with passengers
quests.hint: Think about helping people who are waiting.
quests.explanation: When plans change, clear and honest updates help passengers decide what to do next.
quests.funFact: Airports often use screens and announcements together so travelers do not miss important news.

quests.instruction: In a restaurant, which order shows how a meal reaches the table?
options: Order is taken, kitchen cooks, waiter serves
Waiter serves, kitchen cooks, order is taken
Kitchen cooks, order is taken, waiter serves
quests.correctAnswer: Order is taken, kitchen cooks, waiter serves
quests.hint: Think about what must happen first for each step to make sense.
quests.explanation: A meal starts with the guest's order, then the kitchen prepares it, and finally the waiter brings it to the table.
quests.funFact: Many restaurants use order tickets or screens to pass orders from waiters to cooks.

quests.instruction: In a hospital emergency department, why might a patient who arrived later be seen before someone who arrived earlier?
options: They arrived in a taxi first
They are taller than the others
Their need may be more urgent
quests.correctAnswer: Their need may be more urgent
quests.hint: Think about who needs help most quickly.
quests.explanation: Emergency departments use triage, a way of sorting patients by how urgent their needs are, so those who need help most are treated first.
quests.funFact: The word triage comes from a French word meaning to sort.

quests.instruction: A storm is coming, and a newsroom must report it. Which order makes sense?
options: Presenter shares, reporter gathers facts, editor checks
Reporter gathers facts, editor checks, presenter shares
Editor shares, presenter gathers facts, reporter checks
quests.correctAnswer: Reporter gathers facts, editor checks, presenter shares
quests.hint: Think about finding out, checking, then telling.
quests.explanation: Reporters gather facts, editors check that stories are accurate and clear, and presenters share the news with the audience.
quests.funFact: Newsrooms often double-check important facts before they are shared.

quests.instruction: Why do hospitals, fire stations, and power plants need workers in shifts?
options: They only open during school hours
They have far too many workers
They must be ready day and night
quests.correctAnswer: They must be ready day and night
quests.hint: Think about emergencies that do not wait for morning.
quests.explanation: Important services must work all day and all night, so teams take turns in shifts.
quests.funFact: Some workers switch between day and night shifts, so they plan their sleep carefully.

quests.instruction: At a hotel, who prepares guest rooms by changing sheets, cleaning bathrooms, and restocking supplies?
options: Housekeeper
Receptionist
Hotel Waiter
quests.correctAnswer: Housekeeper
quests.hint: Think about who makes rooms ready for the next guests.
quests.explanation: Housekeepers clean and prepare hotel rooms so guests arrive to a fresh and comfortable space.
quests.funFact: Hotels often track which rooms are clean, which are in use, and which are waiting for service.

quests.instruction: Why do construction workers often hold a short safety meeting before work starts?
options: To decide what everyone will eat
To plan the day and spot hazards
To sort every tool by its color
quests.correctAnswer: To plan the day and spot hazards
quests.hint: Think about preventing accidents before the work begins.
quests.explanation: Safety meetings help teams discuss the day's tasks and any dangers, so everyone knows how to stay safe.
quests.funFact: These short meetings are sometimes called toolbox talks.

quests.instruction: At harvest time, a farm manager has twenty pickers, three trucks, and rain in tomorrow's forecast. What should the manager do?
options: Send everyone home for the week
Plan to harvest before the rain
Wait and let the crops go bad
quests.correctAnswer: Plan to harvest before the rain
quests.hint: Think about using the workers and trucks wisely.
quests.explanation: Farm managers plan teams and transport so ripe crops can be harvested before bad weather arrives.
quests.funFact: Harvest days can start very early so crops are collected while it is cool.

quests.instruction: Early in the morning, a worker fills empty shelves with new products and checks the dates on packages. Who is it?
options: Cashier
Delivery Driver
Shelf Stacker
quests.correctAnswer: Shelf Stacker
quests.hint: Think about who keeps the store's shelves full.
quests.explanation: Shelf stackers restock products and check dates, so customers find fresh items on the shelves.
quests.funFact: Stores often put older products at the front so they are sold first.

quests.instruction: Before each ride starts at a fairground, what must the ride operator check?
options: That every safety bar is locked
That everyone has bought a snack
That the music is playing loudly
quests.correctAnswer: That every safety bar is locked
quests.hint: Think about what keeps riders safe.
quests.explanation: Ride operators make sure everyone is seated and that restraints are locked before starting.
quests.funFact: Many rides have sensors that stop the ride unless the safety restraints are locked.

quests.instruction: Which group of workers might be awake and working at 3 a.m.?
options: Daytime teacher, bus driver, florist
Night nurse, doctor, hospital porter
Bakery cashier, tour guide, referee
quests.correctAnswer: Night nurse, doctor, hospital porter
quests.hint: Think about services that cannot close at night.
quests.explanation: Hospitals care for patients all night, so nurses, doctors, and porters may be on duty. Many other jobs follow daytime hours.
quests.funFact: Some bakers also start work in the middle of the night so bread is fresh by morning.

quests.instruction: Which order follows a passenger through an airport?
options: Check-in agent, security officer, gate agent
Gate agent, check-in agent, security officer
Security officer, gate agent, check-in agent
quests.correctAnswer: Check-in agent, security officer, gate agent
quests.hint: Think about checking in, then security, then boarding.
quests.explanation: Passengers usually check in first, pass through security, and then board at the gate.
quests.funFact: Airports are organized so passengers move through each step in a set order.

quests.instruction: A new worker feels unsure how to use a machine. What is the best choice?
options: Guess how it works and just try it out
Pretend to know and press buttons
Ask an experienced coworker for help
quests.correctAnswer: Ask an experienced coworker for help
quests.hint: Think about learning safely.
quests.explanation: Asking questions keeps people safe and helps them learn the right way to do a task.
quests.funFact: Many workplaces pair new workers with experienced ones for training.

quests.instruction: Which situation shows good teamwork in a hospital?
options: Porter brings a patient, nurse checks, doctor explains
Everyone works alone and never shares information
The cleaner chooses each patient's treatment alone
quests.correctAnswer: Porter brings a patient, nurse checks, doctor explains
quests.hint: Think about each worker doing their own part and passing on information.
quests.explanation: A porter brings the patient, a nurse checks how they are doing, and a doctor explains the plan, so each worker adds a part.
quests.funFact: Hospitals use teams so that no single person has to do everything.

quests.instruction: What do control operators, lifeguards, and security officers have in common?
options: They all spend their days baking bread loaves
They all drive large delivery trucks daily
They watch closely to spot problems early
quests.correctAnswer: They watch closely to spot problems early
quests.hint: Think about what each one must notice.
quests.explanation: Control operators watch systems, lifeguards watch swimmers, and security officers watch places, so each spots problems early.
quests.funFact: Watching carefully often prevents a small problem from becoming a big one.

quests.instruction: During a power cut at a hospital, which action shows good workplace thinking?
options: Close the hospital and send everyone away
Switch to backup power and keep care going
Ignore the alarm and hope for the best
quests.correctAnswer: Switch to backup power and keep care going
quests.hint: Think about essential services staying safe.
quests.explanation: Hospitals have backup systems, such as generators, so equipment and lights can keep working if the main power fails.
quests.funFact: Workers regularly test backup systems to be sure they work when needed.
